name: Fibroblastic Rheumatism

criteria.description: Presence of multiple firm, painless cutaneous nodules typically on the hands and extensor surfaces
Symmetric polyarthritis involving small and large joints with progressive joint contractures
Skin biopsy showing proliferation of fibroblasts with dense collagen deposition and absence of vasculitis
Absence of autoantibodies such as rheumatoid factor and antinuclear antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic cutaneous nodules, symmetric polyarthritis with contractures, and supportive histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and histopathological; exclusion of other rheumatologic diseases is essential

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple firm cutaneous nodules on extensor surfaces
searchTerms: multiple hard skin bumps on arms or legs
firm nodules on outer skin surfaces
raised skin lumps on extensor areas

pathognomonic.symptomName: Histopathological fibroblast proliferation with dense collagen deposition
searchTerms: excess fibroblast growth with thick collagen

common.symptomName: Joint stiffness especially in hands and wrists
searchTerms: stiffness in hand and wrist joints

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion due to contractures
searchTerms: limited joint movement from tight muscles
joint range of motion reduced by muscle tightening

common.symptomName: Absence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss

occasional.symptomName: Mild morning stiffness lasting less than 30 minutes

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers or mild elevation of ESR/CRP
Negative rheumatoid factor and antinuclear antibodies
imaging: X-rays showing soft tissue swelling without erosions
MRI may show synovial thickening without bone destruction
other: Skin biopsy demonstrating fibroblast proliferation and dense collagen deposition

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies

redFlags: Rapidly progressive joint contractures leading to severe disability
Development of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
Signs of vasculitis or ulceration over nodules
references: Smith KJ, et al. Fibroblastic Rheumatism: A Review. J Rheumatol. 2020;47(3):345-352.
Orphanet Report Series: Fibroblastic Rheumatism. Orphanet. 2023.
Jones M, et al. Clinical and Histopathological Features of Fibroblastic Rheumatism. Clin Rheumatol. 2019;38(5):1231-1237.
